This appeal is by State alongwith an application for grant of leave to challenge the judgment of acquittal dated 05.10.2023, passed by the court below in Session Case No.108 of 2011 (State of U.P.
Vs. Vishnu), arising out of Case Crime No. 843 of 2011, under Section 376 IPC, Police Station Maudaha, District- Hamirpur.
As per the prosecution, the informant's minor daughter had gone missing on 18.02.2011.
When he woke up, he found his daughter missing and made attempts to search her but she could not be found.
A missing report was initially lodged.
On 17.02.2011, a telephone call was received from one Vishnu S/o Khyali by informant and it transpired that the victim was in touch with him for more than a month.

Initially on enquiry, Vishnu stated that his phone is misplaced but later it transpired State Of U.P. vs Vishnu S/O Khyali on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108415685/

sentences.text: that the phone was with Vishnu
. An F.I.R. has been lodged on 12.05.2011, nearly three months after the incident.
Case Crime No.843 of 2011 was registered under Sections 363 and 366 I.P.C. against Vishnu.
A charge-sheet was subsequently submitted and after the concerned court took cognizance.
The matter was committed to the Court of Sessions.
Charge was framed against the accused under Section 376 I.P.C. and the trial commenced.
The Court below has examined the testimony of the victim, who has appeared as P.W.-2.
She has admitted that she knew the accused Vishnu.
The accused met the victim when she had gone to the bus station to get samosa.
Vishnu then took her inside a room at the bus station and committed sexual assault upon her.
Out of fear of her father, the victim then left for Farrukhabad and returned after four months.
The medical examination of the victim was conducted in which she was found to be 18 years of age.
The victim has further stated that when she left her house, she came to the railway station from where she travelled to different places by public transport without raising any protest or alarm.
The victim has further stated that after she returned, she has married one Sukhchandra and is living with him.
Trial Court has found material contradictions in the version of the victim, which otherwise was not corroborated by medico legal evidence.

The fact that F.I.R. was lodged nearly three months after disappearance of the victim and the plea of sexual assault was set up only after the return of victim several months later created a doubt in the prosecution case, as per the Court below.
No evidence to corroborate such allegation has, otherwise, been placed on record by the prosecution.
The victim herself admitted that out of fear of her father, she had left on her own.

Since the version of sexual assault has been found to contain material contradictions, which have not been explained, as such the trial Court has granted benefit of doubt to the accused and acquitted the accused.

We have carefully examined the judgment of the court below and upon its examination we find that the view taken by the court below is clearly a permissible view, in the facts of the case, and just because a different view could be taken would ordinarily not be a ground for this Court to interfere with the order of acquittal.

In such circumstances, we find that neither any triable issue is raised before us in this appeal nor any perversity is shown, which may persuade this Court to grant leave to assail the judgment of acquittal.
Prayer made by the State for grant of leave is, accordingly, refused and the appeal, consequently, fails and is dismissed.

Order Date :- 16.12.2023 SP/-
